title: Cybersecurity Analyst Salary Singapore 2026: Pay Guide
metaDescription: Cybersecurity analyst salary Singapore 2026: average SGD 90k-116k, junior 65k-81k, senior 121k-188k. See top employers, certifications and pay-boosting moves.
headline: Cybersecurity Analyst Salary in Singapore 2026: Pay Guide

sections.content:
Singapore is one of Asia's highest-paying markets for cybersecurity talent in 2026. Benchmark aggregators place average total compensation for cybersecurity analysts between 90,000 and 116,000 Singapore dollars per year, though base-salary-only surveys report lower medians near 52,000 dollars.

The gap reflects how compensation is measured: total-compensation benchmarks include bonuses and allowances common at banks and multinationals, while job-posting averages skew toward junior security operations roles. Either way, demand remains intense as financial services, government and tech firms expand security teams.
sections.title: Average Cybersecurity Pay in Singapore for 2026

sections.content:
Junior analysts with zero to two years of experience earn roughly 65,000 to 81,000 Singapore dollars per year. Mid-level analysts with three to five years earn 85,000 to 127,000 dollars, while senior analysts with six or more years earn 121,000 to 188,000 dollars.

The top of the market sits at multinational banks and tech giants: JPMorgan Chase reports median analyst packages above 220,000 dollars, and firms like Apple, Chevron and Bank of America are consistently among the highest payers in the city-state.
sections.title: Salary by Experience Level

sections.content:
Banks, Big Tech and consulting firms pay the most for security talent in Singapore. Financial institutions value incident response, threat intelligence and regulatory compliance skills, while tech companies pay premiums for cloud security and product security engineers.

Government-linked companies and local SMEs pay less but often offer stability and training. Contractors in the market can earn higher monthly rates but give up bonuses, medical coverage and the employer Central Provident Fund contributions that permanent staff receive.
sections.title: Top-Paying Employers and Sectors

sections.content:
Certifications move the needle fastest in this market. CISSP suits governance and management tracks, OSCP proves hands-on penetration testing ability, and cloud security certifications from AWS, Azure or Google Cloud lift pay for infrastructure-focused roles.

Beyond certificates, specializing in scarce areas such as OT security, detection engineering or AI-assisted threat hunting commands premiums. Building a public profile through CTF competitions, bug bounties or security research also strengthens offers, especially when negotiating between competing employers.
